maria_chang: Heads-up — after bringing up the quantized v2 reranker on the ci cluster we see an unexpected MRR spike for tiny candidate sets (k=3,5). Can someone take a quick look?
ajay_patel: spike as in higher MRR than fp32 or just noisy?
devon_lee: it's higher vs fp32 baseline by ~6% on our holdout. suspicious.
sasha_kim: do we have the eval harness config they used on ci? could be different tokenization/normalization.
maria_chang: same harness commit used, but branch enabled PTQ and swapped to `cached-kv` runtime path. posted logs below.
ajay_patel: paste logs?
maria_chang: ```
[2024-08-03T14:12:01Z] model=rerank-v2-quant run_id=ci-2024-08-03 batch=1 k=5 mrr=0.412 fp32_mrr=0.388
[2024-08-03T14:12:12Z] model=rerank-v2-quant run_id=ci-2024-08-03 k=50 mrr=0.276 fp32_mrr=0.281
```
kai: interesting that the effect flips for k=50. smells like candidate ordering or truncation interacting with quantization.
sasha_kim: could be padding/truncation differences when we pack short docs into sequences; int8 kernel may change early-stop or attention masking edge-case.
devon_lee: another angle: our holdout is mix of short queries (one token) and long docs. For small k the top candidate is often a near-exact title match — maybe quantization sharpened the scores.
ajay_patel: we should check score distribution (ties, gaps) and parity of softmax temps. also confirm random seeds.
maria_chang: ran quick scoring dump (top-5) for 200 examples, attached in gist: https://gist.github.com/ci-dumps/abcd1234 (private)
eval-bot: automated-eval: sample=200 k=5 mean_mrr_quant=0.413 mean_mrr_fp32=0.387 pval=0.03 (wilcoxon)
sasha_kim: pval low but sample small. maybe cherry. what's the sampling proto (curated vs uniform)?
maria_chang: used our standard dev holdout (time-based split, deduped anchors). 40% short queries (<4 tokens).
kai: quick experiment idea: compare with MS MARCO dev subset and with internal dev where we strip titles vs keep titles. if spike only when titles present it's formatting-related.
devon_lee: also try normalizing docs by removing punctuation and lowercasing to see if tokenizer subtleties cause reorder.
ajay_patel: agree. can we also test varying candidate set sizes and fixed-length padding: pad_to=512 vs pad_to=128.
sasha_kim: I'll run a small matrix: dataset in {internal_holdout, msmarco_sample}, pad in {128,512}, k in {5,50}, model in {fp32,quant} — will post results. ETA ~2h.
maria_chang: thanks. also please check the eval harness uses same tokenization codepath as prod; earlier a refactor made a `TokenizerV2` only used in ci.
ai: @sasha_kim noted tokenization path mismatch, adding to checklist.
devon_lee: if it persists after normalization, we might be seeing quantization-induced calibration shift — consider rescaling logits before softmax (temperature tweak) as a guard.
ajay_patel: add a quick ablation: calibrate quant scores by multiplying by 0.98..1.02 range and recompute MRR. see if small rescale flips improvement.
sasha_kim: running that too. also logging top-1 examples where quant wins and where fp32 wins for manual inspection.
maria_chang: if it's a real quality win for tiny-k, we should be careful — customers often use k=1-5. but if it's a regression on larger candidate sets we may need fallback policy: quant for small-k, fp32 otherwise.
kai: routing policy is possible but prefer understanding root cause first.
eval-bot: queued job: matrix-run-1739123456 started (job id q-789). will post summary when complete. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
